# refactor(dx): replace Awilix with explicit factories and wire observers in composition

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

Builds on the public application API: `src/app/api.ts` exists, no command or use case receives a
container, and `src/app/container.ts` is the only production file that imports Awilix. If
`src/app/api.ts` is missing, the base branch is too old; stop and say so.

## What

The application describes the capabilities it needs and never builds or looks up concrete
implementations itself. All construction and wiring happens at startup.

## Why

App currently assembles adapters and observers through a container. That hides what each operation
really needs and lets infrastructure creep into use cases.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases), `cli` (commands) and `composition`
(builds adapters, binds operations, starts the executable).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR, except that the construction decision below is final.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Decision: remove Awilix

Build adapters with explicit typed factories in `src/composition`, and keep the lifecycle wrappers in
`src/app/lifecycle.ts`. Do not build a registry, resolver or autowiring in its place. Copy this decision
and its reasons into the PR description.

A comparison of today's code, Awilix confined to composition, and explicit factories found:

- All three behave the same. The choice is about visible dependencies, not a bug being fixed.
- Production registers no Awilix disposers, so every container `dispose()` releases nothing. Cleanup is
  done by `withResource`, `releaseInOrder` and `releasingOnPanic`, which stay.
- A missing or mistyped dependency in a container factory's parameter compiles and fails at run time.
  With factories it is a compile error.
- With child scopes, marking `openSession` as a singleton compiles, and init then opens sandboxes with
  the old config and credentials.
- Overriding a registration after something has read it leaves part of the graph on the old value.
- Awilix disposal cannot follow jig's cleanup rules: it ignores a returned `Err` and reports failures by
  rejecting. The wrappers would be needed either way.

## Target

Spec sections: "Composition", "Application preparation and resource lifetime" (observers),
"Dependency lint", "Acceptance evidence" items 3, 5 and 8. The spec and several guides still call the
mechanism undecided; the decision above settles it.

- `src/app/container.ts` (22 adapter and observer imports) mixes adapter construction, scopes, lifecycle
  policy and execution preparation: `openRunRuntime`, `openSandboxRuntime`, `createAppContainer`,
  `runCapabilitiesOf`, the private `openRunScope`, `AppCradle` and `RunCradle`. Delete it.
- `src/app/sandbox-image.ts` (3 adapter imports: the image recipe, `readSandboxDockerfile` and `AGENTS`)
  and `src/app/observed-events.ts` (1 observer import) are app's other infrastructure imports.
- Composition gains the factories that implement `RunRuntime` and `SandboxRuntime` for the operations
  bound in `src/composition/main.ts`. Pass each factory only what it reads; do not make one shared bag
  of dependencies.
- App keeps the policy now in `openRunScope`: retrying a sandbox start with `transientRetryPolicy`,
  releasing a partial acquisition, and closing the session before disposing the scope. It works over
  lazy parts that composition supplies.
- These behaviors must hold afterwards. Each is covered once, in the spec of the module that owns it;
  keep the existing test where one already covers it, and add one only for a gap:
  - Building a runtime opens nothing. Status and an ended run open no sandbox, image or run log.
  - Two runs in one process share the console log, and keep their events, metrics and workspace apart.
  - Each `sandboxFor` uses the config and environment it was given, including its image name and
    credentials. It shares the runtime's log, and earlier sandboxes keep their own settings.
  - A start that may pass is retried and then opens, or returns its last failure. A configuration failure
    is not retried. Either failure leaves nothing open.
  - A panic while opening releases the scope. A panic while assembling it closes the session, then
    releases the scope. Both propagate as thrown.
  - Release order is session, scope, telemetry, run lock. A throwaway sandbox closes before its branch is
    removed. A cleanup failure replaces success and never replaces a work failure.
- App's lifecycle wrappers own lifecycle policy through supplied capabilities (lazy
  factories, scope capabilities). Domain, steps, flow and use cases never see a container,
  registration keys, resolution or scope APIs. Keep deferred construction where it matters, and
  avoid an application-wide dependency bag.
- Composition constructs concrete adapters and attaches observers (`src/observers/*`). App requests
  logs and events through ports only. Move the plain metrics/report data that app responses need
  into portable contracts, so app does not import observers.
- Keep custom run-store module loading: the adapter validates the module and its values, app picks
  required stores by policy, composition supplies the implementations.
- Observer isolation: an ordinary observer exception is reported and the other observers are still
  notified; a panic propagates.
- Shutdown flushes output after resources close.
- Lint: app cannot import `adapters`, `observers` or `cli`. Delete `awilixOnlyInApp` from
  `eslint.config.js` (two uses), and restrict Pino/OpenTelemetry to concrete reporting
  and wiring areas. Add fixtures.
- Specs that build the container: `src/app/container.spec.ts`, `src/app/run-jig.integration.spec.ts`
  (16 calls to `runCapabilitiesOf`, built through one `setup`) and
  `src/app/implement-issue.integration.spec.ts` (one `setup`). Move the
  behaviors `container.spec.ts` covers to specs beside their new owners, then delete it. Keep every
  assertion in the other two; only how they build the run changes. Specs need to replace the sandbox
  opener, images, log and retry settings (the fixed retry delay is 5 seconds).
- Remove the `awilix` dependency from `package.json` and the lockfile.
- Update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` and
  `CLAUDE.md` (current picks), `.claude/rules/callee-owns-its-rules.md`,
  `.claude/rules/testing-conventions.md`, and the statements in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`
  that call the mechanism undecided.

Out of scope: closing the run log file when its scope is released. It stays open until the process exits
today, and closing it is a behavior change. Keep the `dispose` contracts on `RunRuntime`,
`SandboxRuntime` and `RunScope`, even where production has nothing to release.

## Done when

- [ ] `grep -rnE "from '\.\./(adapters|observers)/" src/app --include='*.ts' --exclude='*.spec.ts'` finds
      nothing, and lint enforces it. Specs in `src/app` may keep importing adapters.
- [ ] `grep -rniE "awilix" src scripts package.json package-lock.json eslint.config.js` finds nothing.
- [ ] `grep -rnE "#49" src scripts .dependency-cruiser.mjs CONTRIBUTING.md .claude/rules docs/architecture.html docs/workflow-ownership.md docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`
      finds no text that calls the construction mechanism undecided.
- [ ] `src/app/lifecycle.spec.ts` and the "runJig over supplied capabilities" tests in
      `src/app/run-jig.spec.ts` pass unchanged, and every behavior listed under Target is
      covered once, by an existing spec or a new one.
- [ ] Observer failure isolation and panic propagation are tested.
- [ ] The built executable's `--help` and `github implement --help` work, and output is flushed after resources close.
- [ ] The full verification below passes, including `npm run validate`.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run validate
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.



Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/59

context.repoSummary: The prerequisite src/app/api.ts exists and exports capability-based operations and runtime contracts. src/composition/main.ts already binds operations and owns executable startup, but imports openRunRuntime/openSandboxRuntime from src/app/container.ts. That container combines Awilix registration, concrete adapters, observer attachment, lazy run scopes, sandbox retry and partial-acquisition cleanup. Explicit composition factories must replace construction while app retains lifecycle policy through src/app/lifecycle.ts and supplied capabilities. Other infrastructure leaks are app/sandbox-image.ts and app/observed-events.ts; portable metrics/report contracts already exist in ports/run-records.ts. Observer exception isolation and panic propagation already have coverage in observed-events.spec.ts. container.spec.ts covers scope construction, retry exhaustion, telemetry, panic cleanup and sandbox configuration; run-jig.integration.spec.ts and implement-issue.integration.spec.ts override container registrations in their setup helpers. Preserve their assertions while replacing setup. Dependency enforcement currently uses .dependency-cruiser.mjs, .dependency-cruiser.specs.mjs and scripts/lint-dependencies.integration.spec.ts; the request's scripts/check-dependencies files are absent. Existing fixtures explicitly permit app adapter construction and need revision alongside ESLint's awilixOnlyInApp restriction. Architecture, ownership guides, CONTRIBUTUTING-related code maps and the application-boundaries spec still defer construction to #49; the request settles that decision. Validation uses npm run validate with pinned Node 26.13.0 and includes build, typecheck, lint, dependency checks, formatting, coverage, integration tests, duplication and secret scanning. Preserve lazy acquisition, cleanup order, sandbox-only agents, credential handling and CLI behavior; no implementation changes were made.
